kind: a production-binding design manifest: the statement WalletWall would have to bind, the threats, the trust layers, the candidate architectures and the recommendation, the encoding and replay contracts, the identity lifecycle, the PA3D residue dispositions, the gates, the failure semantics and the invariants a later, separately authorized implementation lane would build and test. Design only: it changes no contract, deploys nothing, proves nothing, and establishes no binding.

carriedForward: one real v2 proof was generated (Groth16, SP1 6.3.1, circuit v6.1.0) of the designated program mldsa65-withdrawal-d1 from the manifest's source commit debed530, in 646 s on one 16-thread host
the proof was independently verified by the designated runtime from a fresh process: ACCEPTED, one check, selector 0x4388a21c
the statement reproduced the expected public values: the 160-byte journal's sha256 64e08d05… equals the fixture-derived expectation
proof-byte determinism was NOT claimed: the PA3B and PA3D proofs of one statement differ in bytes, as Groth16 proving is randomized
the attribution chain validated: 15 of 15 links hold, from the source commit through manifest, attestation, run, proof, verification and record to the qualified observer and the declared boundary
the negative controls passed: NC-V1..NC-V5 refused by the designated runtime, NC-R1..NC-R12 refused by the record validator

process and network attribution was only PARTIAL: assurance CONTINUOUS_PARTIALLY_ATTRIBUTED, 162 attempts, 237 refused packets, 19 unattributed kernel events, 10 sends of unseen destination, 3 other-namespace sends, 0 unknown outcomes
Docker Desktop was active during the proof (PA3D-F4): its service VM accounts for the 3 other-namespace sends, 192.168.65.x over vsock
the measurement tool has a shutdown defect (PA3D-F1): it keeps a readline on stdin after writing its observation and is killed by the observer's 600 s guard, with a misleading stderr line
chronyd activity existed: 54 refused time-sync attempts inside the window, every one refused; the host clock ran free
the acquisition gate does not bind the complete Node dependency tree: package-lock integrity and the installed node_modules are outside the exercise manifest's digests
the PA3D lane validators (validate:sp1-pa3d-manifest, validate:sp1-pa3d-record) are not yet wired into canonical CI; their logic runs there only through the mocha suite

the implementation receipt still reports PRODUCTION_SP1_BINDING_STATUS = NOT_ESTABLISHED with three prerequisites unmet: the two-host canonical rebuild (INSUFFICIENT_HOSTS), a registered active wrapper (0 registrations) and owner review

statement.subject: The holder of the ML-DSA-65 credential registered for a vault owner authorized exactly one Vault operation, identified by the consumer's EIP-712 digest: a Withdrawal (vaultOwner, recipient, amount, nonce, deadline, vaultMode) or a RotateCredentials (vaultOwner, newEcdsaSigner, newPQPublicKey, nonce, deadline). The proof replaces an on-chain ML-DSA-65 verification, nothing more: it is the post-quantum conjunct of the Vault's authorization, never a policy decision, a state transition or an evidence assertion. This is the existing Vault semantic (IPQCVerifier.verify(digest, publicKey, proof) at every PQ-gated site); no new semantic is invented for SP1.
statement.relation: exists signature: ML-DSA-65.Verify(publicKey, digest, ctx = empty, signature) = true, with keccak256(publicKey) = pkHash and keccak256(signature) = sigHash, committed as the 160-byte journal (digest, pkHash, sigHash, chainId, verifierAddress). The guest (zkvm/guest/src/bin/withdrawal.rs) is digest-agnostic: it never parses the operation, so every operation-specific fact binds through the digest the consumer computes.
consumerPath: WalletWallVault computes digest = _hashTypedDataV4(structHash(request)) from the caller's typed request, under EIP712("WalletWallVault", "1") whose domain fixes chainId and verifyingContract

WalletWallVault checks deadline (DeadlineExpired), nonce (InvalidNonce), mode (VaultModeMismatch), balance, then calls pqVerifier.verify(digest, vault.pqPublicKey, pqSignature) where vault.pqPublicKey is the credential registered for that owner

ZKMLDSAVerifier.verify returns false if halted; decodes abi.encode(bytes publicValues, bytes proofBytes); requires publicValues.length == 160 and proofBytes.length > 0; decodes (bytes32, bytes32, bytes32, uint64, address) with ABI validation; requires committedDigest == digest, committedPkHash == keccak256(publicKey), uint256(committedChainId) == block.chainid, committedVerifier == address(this)

ZKMLDSAVerifier calls ISP1Verifier(SP1_VERIFIER).verifyProof(PROGRAM_VKEY, publicValues, proofBytes) inside try/catch: SP1_VERIFIER is pinned at construction to Succinct's Groth16 SP1Verifier v6.1.0 by runtime code hash, PROGRAM_VKEY is immutable; the verifier derives sha256(publicValues) masked to 253 bits and checks the Groth16 proof against (PROGRAM_VKEY, that digest); any revert is false
WalletWallVault reverts InvalidPQSignature on false; on true it consumes the nonce in the same transaction and executes or queues exactly the request it hashed

publicInputs.name: operationId
publicInputs.today: journal word 0 (withdrawalDigest) == digest, checked by ZKMLDSAVerifier; operationId == digest in WalletWallVault
publicInputs.why: The digest is the statement's whole operation identity: it is the one value the guest signs over and the one value the consumer computes itself, so it is the join between the proof and the executed operation.

publicInputs.name: chainId
publicInputs.today: journal word 3 (uint64) compared full-width with block.chainid (SP1-P1 F-1); also inside the EIP-712 domain of the digest
publicInputs.why: A proof routed to another chain must fail: two independent bindings exist, the journal word (checked by the wrapper) and the EIP-712 domain (recomputed by OpenZeppelin EIP712 when the chain id changes).

publicInputs.name: vaultAddress
publicInputs.today: verifyingContract in the EIP-712 domain separator of the digest; the Vault computes the digest itself and never accepts one from the caller
publicInputs.why: Another Vault with the same owner, recipient, amount and nonce produces a different digest, so a proof made for one Vault cannot verify for another (PB-2). The journal does not carry it separately because the digest already does and the guest cannot check it.

publicInputs.name: verifierAddress
publicInputs.today: journal word 4 == address(this) in ZKMLDSAVerifier
publicInputs.why: One program and one chain can host several wrapper deployments; the word pins the proof to the wrapper it was made for, so a proof addressed to a halted or superseded wrapper dies with it.

publicInputs.name: pkHash
publicInputs.today: journal word 1 == keccak256(publicKey), where the Vault passes vault.pqPublicKey, the credential registered for the owner it looked up; at rotateCredentials it additionally passes the incoming newPQPublicKey for a second proof over the same rotation digest (possession of the new credential)
publicInputs.why: The proof must be about the credential the consumer names (the registered one, or at rotation the incoming one whose possession is proven), not any ML-DSA key the prover chose; hashing the 1,952-byte key keeps the journal fixed-width.

publicInputs.name: vaultOwner
publicInputs.today: Withdrawal.vaultOwner / RotateCredentials.vaultOwner in the struct hash; the Vault also binds the owner through vault.pqPublicKey
publicInputs.why: Cross-user replay (T04) needs the owner inside the statement; two owners registering one key still produce different digests.

publicInputs.name: recipient
publicInputs.today: Withdrawal.recipient in the struct hash; the Vault pays request.recipient, the field it hashed
publicInputs.why: An altered destination (T08) changes the digest and therefore the journal's first word; PB-3.

publicInputs.name: amount
publicInputs.today: Withdrawal.amount in the struct hash; the Vault transfers request.amount
publicInputs.why: An altered amount (T09) changes the digest; PB-4.

publicInputs.name: nonce
publicInputs.today: Withdrawal.nonce / RotateCredentials.nonce in the struct hash; the Vault requires request.nonce == vault.nonce and sets vault.nonce = request.nonce + 1 in the same transaction
publicInputs.why: The per-owner nonce is the replay nullifier (T01, PB-6): one digest, one execution.

publicInputs.name: deadline
publicInputs.today: Withdrawal.deadline / RotateCredentials.deadline in the struct hash; the Vault requires block.timestamp <= deadline (DeadlineExpired)
publicInputs.why: Freshness: an unconsumed proof expires. A deadline is the only time binding the statement can afford, because proving takes about eleven minutes.

publicInputs.name: vaultMode
publicInputs.today: Withdrawal.vaultMode in the struct hash; the Vault requires request.vaultMode == uint8(vault.mode)
publicInputs.why: A proof made under one credential mode must not survive a mode change: the mode decides which conjuncts the Vault demands.

publicInputs.name: operationType
publicInputs.today: WITHDRAWAL_TYPEHASH vs ROTATE_CREDENTIALS_TYPEHASH as the struct hash's first word
publicInputs.why: Cross-operation replay (T05): a withdrawal signature cannot authorize a rotation because the type hash differs; the guest cannot know the type, so the consumer's typed data carries it.

publicInputs.name: domainSeparator
publicInputs.today: EIP712("WalletWallVault", "1") domain: name, version, chainId, verifyingContract, hashed into every digest by _hashTypedDataV4
publicInputs.why: The domain separator is what makes the digest a WalletWallVault digest rather than any 32 bytes; it is inside the statement already. A journal-level domain word is not needed while PROGRAM_VKEY separates programs (see encoding.nextGeneration).

publicInputs.name: programIdentity
publicInputs.today: PROGRAM_VKEY, immutable in ZKMLDSAVerifier, passed to ISP1Verifier.verifyProof; the Groth16 statement binds the proof to the vkey
publicInputs.why: The program is bound by the verifier's public input, not by a journal word: a journal that named its own vkey would be circular, since only the vkey's verifier would check it (T11, PB-5).

publicInputs.name: verifierVersion
publicInputs.today: SP1_VERIFIER_CODEHASH pins the runtime code of SP1Verifier v6.1.0 at construction; proofBytes[0:4] must equal the verifier's VERIFIER_HASH selector 0x4388a21c or verifyProof reverts
publicInputs.why: A proof for another SP1 version or another Groth16 circuit must not verify; the pin excludes the owner-mutable gateway and any accept-all contract (T20).

publicInputs.name: signatureHash
publicInputs.today: journal word 2 is bound by the proof (sha256 of the journal) but deliberately unchecked by the consumer (SP1-P1 F-2)
publicInputs.why: Any valid ML-DSA signature over the digest authorizes; which signature was used adds no authorization fact. It MAY stay as an audit handle; no consumer may rely on it, and the next program generation may drop it.

publicInputs.name: asset
publicInputs.today: WalletWallVault holds one asset (native ETH); the Withdrawal struct has no asset field
publicInputs.why: There is no asset to alter in the v1 Vault. Any multi-asset consumer (the vNext kernel's spend plane) MUST put the asset identifier into its operation digest; PB-12 makes that a requirement, so the classification becomes MUST_BIND via EIP712_DIGEST there.

publicInputs.name: tokenContract
publicInputs.today: no ERC-20 path in WalletWallVault
publicInputs.why: Same as asset: the token contract address is the asset identifier of a multi-asset consumer and binds through that consumer's digest, never through the guest.

publicInputs.name: sourceWallet
publicInputs.today: the source of a withdrawal is the Vault's own balance for vaultOwner
publicInputs.why: The source is implied by vaultAddress and vaultOwner, both bound; a separate word would duplicate them.

publicInputs.name: policyEngine
publicInputs.today: the Vault calls policyEngine.check at admission and revalidate at finalization (STATICCALL, fail-closed), recording policyEngineAtQueue
publicInputs.why: Policy is admission, not authorization. Binding the engine's identity into the proof would make every proof stale on a policy rotation and would let a prover assert a policy fact the engine must decide live (T06, T15).

publicInputs.name: policySnapshot
publicInputs.today: not part of the statement
publicInputs.why: A policy snapshot in the proof is both stale by construction (eleven-minute proving) and a false assurance: the Vault's revalidate at finalization is the only policy verdict that counts.

publicInputs.name: blockNumberOrHash
publicInputs.today: not part of the statement
publicInputs.why: Proving takes about 646 s on the exercised host; a block binding would expire every proof before it lands and would couple the statement to reorgs. Freshness is the deadline; replay is the nonce (T16).

publicInputs.name: timestamp
publicInputs.today: only the deadline is bound; no issue timestamp exists in the statement
publicInputs.why: An issue time is unverifiable by the consumer and adds nothing the deadline does not; a bound issue time would also leak the prover's clock (chronyd residue).

publicInputs.name: stateRoot
publicInputs.today: not part of the statement
publicInputs.why: The proof attests a signature, not Vault state; balance, mode and nonce are read by the Vault at execution, which is the only place they are current (T07).

publicInputs.name: programVersionString
publicInputs.today: not part of the statement
publicInputs.why: A human-readable version is not an identity; PROGRAM_VKEY is. Any version word a prover writes is a claim the verifier cannot check.

privateInputs.name: publicKey (ML-DSA-65, 1,952 bytes)
privateInputs.why: Only keccak256(publicKey) is public; the consumer already holds the key (vault.pqPublicKey) and recomputes the hash, so disclosure through the proof is unnecessary. Zero knowledge is used here for succinctness, not secrecy: the key is public on chain.

privateInputs.name: signature (ML-DSA-65, 3,309 bytes)
privateInputs.why: The signature is what the proof replaces: verifying it on chain is what costs too much. keccak256(signature) is committed but unchecked; the bytes never leave the prover.

verificationMeans: Layer A: Succinct's Groth16 SP1Verifier v6.1.0, at the code the wrapper pinned, accepted the proof for (PROGRAM_VKEY, sha256(publicValues) masked to 253 bits) on this chain's precompiles

Layer B: the proof was made by a program whose SP1 verifying key is PROGRAM_VKEY, the designated mldsa65-withdrawal-d1 guest, under the soundness of SP1's Groth16 wrap and the v6.1.0 circuit's trusted setup
Layer C: that program committed exactly these 160 bytes, and the wrapper found the digest, the credential hash, the chain id and its own address in them

Under those assumptions and the correctness of the guest's ML-DSA-65 implementation: someone who held a signature valid under the owner's registered credential over this Vault's digest for this operation produced the proof
verificationDoesNotMean: that the operation is admitted: deadline, nonce, mode, balance, policy check and revalidate, the large-transaction queue delay and the pause are the Vault's, evaluated at execution

that the signer is the owner in any sense other than holding the registered credential: credential compromise is outside the statement, which is why generation 1 keeps the ECDSA floor (Hybrid) and rejects PqOnly

that the program is correct: PROGRAM_VKEY identifies the designated ELF; whether that ELF implements ML-DSA-65 correctly is provenance and review evidence, not something the proof shows (soundness is NOT_ESTABLISHED_BY_PROVENANCE)

which prover, host or source checkout made the proof: production binding never consults prover provenance; PA3D's attribution residue is evidence about one exercise, not an input to on-chain soundness
that WalletWall offers quantum-safe production custody, or that PRODUCTION_SP1_BINDING is anything but NOT_ESTABLISHED

trustLayers.name: cryptographic proof validity
trustLayers.question: Did the Groth16 proof verify?
trustLayers.establishedBy: ISP1Verifier(SP1_VERIFIER).verifyProof on the chain's precompiles; SP1_VERIFIER pinned by runtime code hash to SP1Verifier v6.1.0; the verifier's VK_ROOT and the proof's 4-byte selector
trustLayers.transition: A valid proof is valid for a verifying key and a public-values digest, nothing else: without Layer B's PROGRAM_VKEY it says only that some SP1 program committed some bytes.

trustLayers.name: program identity
trustLayers.question: Was it the designated WalletWall program?
trustLayers.establishedBy: PROGRAM_VKEY immutable in the wrapper, equal to the designation mldsa65-withdrawal-d1 (CI subject check); the Groth16 public input binds the proof to that vkey
trustLayers.transition: Knowing the program says what relation holds, not for which values: Layer C's journal supplies the values, and only their sha256 is bound by the proof, so the consumer must still parse and compare them.

trustLayers.name: statement identity
trustLayers.question: Were the intended public values actually proven?
trustLayers.establishedBy: publicValues.length == 160; ABI-validated decode of five static words; digest, pkHash, chainId and verifierAddress compared by the wrapper; sha256(publicValues) is the verifier's public input
trustLayers.transition: On chain the path ends here: the Vault learns true or false. Layer D is off-chain evidence about where the program and the proof came from; it is never an input to verify().

trustLayers.name: provenance
trustLayers.question: Can WalletWall identify which source, program and input produced the statement?
trustLayers.establishedBy: the designation (source commit, ELF sha256, vkey), the canonical build and its two-host rebuild (unmet), the wrapper registry, the PA3D exercise manifest, attestation, run observation and record (15 of 15 links)
trustLayers.transition: Provenance tells reviewers which program is behind PROGRAM_VKEY and how one proof was made; it cannot tell whether this particular proof may be used now, which is Layer E's freshness.

trustLayers.name: freshness and replay protection
trustLayers.question: Can the proof be reused where it should not be?
trustLayers.establishedBy: nonce, deadline and vaultMode inside the digest; chainId and verifierAddress in the journal; the Vault consumes the nonce in the transaction that accepts the proof
trustLayers.transition: An unreplayed, in-date authorization is still only an authorization: Layer F decides whether the Vault admits the operation at all.

trustLayers.name: policy authorization
trustLayers.question: Does the proven result satisfy the Vault's production policy?
trustLayers.establishedBy: policyEngine.check at admission and revalidate at finalization (STATICCALL, fail-closed), the large-transaction queue delay, treasury quorum, pause; none of these is in the statement by design
trustLayers.transition: Admission decides whether an operation runs; Layer G decides that what runs is the operation that was proven.

trustLayers.name: execution binding
trustLayers.question: Does the executed operation match the operation proven?
trustLayers.establishedBy: the Vault executes request.recipient and request.amount, the very fields it hashed into the digest it verified; queued operations are stored under operationId and finalized from the stored request
trustLayers.transition: Terminal. A valid proof at Layer A is never described as sufficient for Layer G: six transitions separate them, each with its own check and its own failure.

trustAssumptions: soundness of SP1 6.x's Groth16 wrap and the v6.1.0 circuit's trusted setup (Succinct), as deployed in SP1Verifier v6.1.0 at code hash 0xcceb864c…
correctness of the chain's bn254 precompiles (per-chain execution check measures verdicts, not soundness)
correctness of the guest's ML-DSA-65 implementation and of the fixture-derived expectation it is compared with (provenance and review; NOT_ESTABLISHED_BY_PROVENANCE)
keccak256 and sha256 collision resistance (journal hashes, the verifier's public-values digest)
EIP-712 domain separation as implemented by OpenZeppelin EIP712 in WalletWallVault
the ECDSA floor remains required in generation 1 (Hybrid): the PQ verdict is a conjunct, never the sole authenticator (I-NO-SOLE-EXTERNAL-AUTHENTICATOR)

Vault governance (the contract owner) proposes verifier rotations honestly or is caught within the 172,800 s delay, which is the users' exit window; the halt principal is independent of governance and can only deny
the designated ELF is what the designation says: a two-host canonical rebuild is required before any identity may become QUALIFIED, and it is unmet today

threats.name: proof replay
threats.binding: The digest commits the per-owner nonce; the Vault requires request.nonce == vault.nonce and advances it in the transaction that accepts the proof (withdraw, queueWithdrawal, rotateCredentials). A second submission of the same proof fails InvalidNonce before the verifier is consulted. Tests: WalletWallVault 'fail on replay with the same nonce', rotation 'cannot be replayed once the nonce has advanced'.

threats.name: cross-chain replay
threats.binding: Two independent bindings: the journal's chainId word is compared full-width with block.chainid in ZKMLDSAVerifier (SP1-P1 F-1), and the EIP-712 domain of the digest carries the chain id, recomputed by OpenZeppelin EIP712 if the chain id changes. Test: ZKMLDSAVerifierProgramIdentity 'refuses a journal committing another chain id'.

threats.name: cross-Vault replay
threats.binding: verifyingContract in the EIP-712 domain makes another Vault's digest differ; the Vault computes the digest itself from the typed request and never accepts a caller-supplied digest (PB-11). The journal's verifierAddress word additionally pins the wrapper deployment. The wrapper is shared by several consumers by design, so this binding is the consumers' typed-data discipline, which PB-11's gate must test for every consumer.

threats.name: cross-user replay
threats.binding: vaultOwner is a field of both typed structs, and pkHash must equal keccak256 of the credential registered for the owner the Vault looked up (vault.pqPublicKey). Two owners registering the same key still produce different digests.

threats.name: cross-operation replay
threats.binding: WITHDRAWAL_TYPEHASH and ROTATE_CREDENTIALS_TYPEHASH differ, so a withdrawal digest is never a rotation digest; both structs carry the nonce. Test: ZKMLDSAWithdrawalRelationConsumers 'a withdrawal signature cannot authorize a credential rotation'. The guest is digest-agnostic, so this protection is entirely the consumer's typed data (PB-11, PB-12).

threats.name: stale policy replay
threats.binding: Policy is excluded from the statement (policyEngine and policySnapshot are MUST_NOT_BIND). The proof cannot carry a looser policy because it carries none: the Vault's engine decides at check and again at revalidate with the recorded policyEngineAtQueue, fail-closed on STATICCALL failure.

threats.name: stale state replay
threats.binding: Balance, mode, nonce and deadline are read by the Vault at execution; the proof attests a signature, not state. The nonce stops re-execution, the deadline bounds the proof's life, and vaultMode in the digest voids proofs made under a previous mode.

threats.name: altered destination
threats.binding: recipient is hashed into the digest; the Vault pays request.recipient, the field it hashed; any other recipient changes the digest and the journal's first word, so the proof fails at the wrapper. Test: 'one observed withdrawal signature cannot authorize a different withdrawal'.

threats.name: altered amount
threats.binding: amount is hashed into the digest and the Vault transfers request.amount; same mechanism as T08.

threats.name: altered asset
threats.binding: WalletWallVault holds one asset (native ETH), so there is no asset to alter; by construction the threat is empty for the v1 Vault.
threats.residual: Any multi-asset consumer (the vNext kernel's spend plane) must put the asset identifier into its operation digest; the design requires it (PB-12) but no such typed data is frozen in the repository today, so the binding is a requirement on the production candidate, not an existing check.

threats.name: verifier/program substitution
threats.binding: PROGRAM_VKEY is immutable per wrapper; SP1_VERIFIER is pinned at construction to the v6.1.0 runtime code hash, which excludes the owner-mutable gateway, mocks and accept-all contracts; the Vault records pqVerifierIdentity = keccak256(codehash, vkey) at install and changes it only through the 172,800 s rotation guarded by VerifierRotationGuard. Tests: ZKMLDSAVerifierProgramIdentity (ACVP-program proofs refused both ways), 'rejects an EOA as the SP1 verifier'.

threats.name: old-program downgrade
threats.residual: Today the consumer refuses only a HALTED identity (VerifierRotationGuard); a superseded-but-not-halted wrapper, or a fresh wrapper of an old PROGRAM_VKEY, can be re-installed through the owner's timelocked rotation. The design closes this with the identity register (lifecycle: DEPRECATED and REVOKED identities are refused at proposal and at apply, DEPRECATED never returns to ACTIVE) and PB-7; until that is built, downgrade resistance rests on governance plus the 2-day exit window.

threats.name: a proof made for development infrastructure reused in production
threats.binding: A proof made against a development chain or wrapper carries that chain id and that verifier address in its journal, and fails the wrapper's comparisons on any other deployment; a development program (the ACVP guest, a modified guest) has another vkey. The prover's environment is otherwise irrelevant to validity: production binding depends on soundness, not on who ran the prover, which is why PA3D's attribution residue does not bear on Layer A to C.

threats.name: a valid proof paired with wrong public values
threats.binding: SP1Verifier derives sha256(publicValues) (masked to 253 bits) and uses it as the Groth16 public input together with the vkey, so any change to the 160 bytes fails verification; the wrapper additionally compares four of the five words with its own context. Tests: NC-V3 (wrong public values refused), 'rejects a withdrawal if the digest is tampered in the proof'.

threats.name: a proof made under a different policy version
threats.binding: The guest has no policy input and the statement carries no policy fact, so a proof is policy-version-free; admission is decided by the engine current at check and revalidate (T06).

threats.name: stale or forked chain data
threats.binding: The statement depends on no chain data (no block, no state root), so staleness cannot be exploited through the proof; on a fork that changes its chain id the journal word and the EIP-712 domain both fail.
threats.residual: A fork that keeps the chain id replays the authorization on both forks, exactly as the owner's ECDSA signature does; the nonce is consumed independently on each. Bounded by the deadline and equal to the ECDSA floor's exposure: an accepted boundary, not a binding.

threats.name: source-commit substitution
threats.binding: On chain only PROGRAM_VKEY matters. The designation binds source commit to ELF sha256 to vkey in committed evidence with a CI subject check; the PA3D record ties one proof to the source commit through 15 links.
threats.residual: The link from source to ELF is reproducibility evidence: the canonical two-host rebuild is unmet (INSUFFICIENT_HOSTS), so a reviewer today has one build's word that the designated ELF is the designated source. The lifecycle makes that rebuild a condition of QUALIFIED (PB-18).

threats.name: malformed encoding ambiguity
threats.binding: publicValues.length != 160 or empty proofBytes reverts InvalidProof inside decodeProofPayload, caught as false; the five words are decoded with Solidity's ABI decoder, which rejects non-canonical uint64 and address words; malformed dynamic offsets in the (bytes, bytes) payload are caught the same way. Tests: 'returns false for malformed ABI proof payloads', NC-V4 truncated proof, NC-V5 foreign selector.

threats.name: canonicalization differences
threats.binding: One encoding, static ABI (bytes32, bytes32, bytes32, uint64, address), is produced by the guest and expected by the TypeScript prover client and the Solidity decoder; PA3D's STATEMENT_TO_PUBLIC_VALUES link reproduced the fixture-derived expectation through the guest, a cross-implementation check of the canonical form. The design adds that check as a CI fixture gate (G-02) so it is enforced on every change, not once.

threats.name: verifier upgrade ambiguity
threats.binding: A consumer has exactly one pqVerifier at a time; a rotation is proposed, waits 172,800 s, is re-checked for code at apply and expires after 14 days unused (Sp1Td2VerifierRotation). After apply, proofs addressed to the old wrapper fail its verifierAddress word, so there is no window in which two identities authorize; already-queued operations finalize without re-verification.
threats.residual: Lifecycle states are not expressed on chain: the consumer cannot distinguish ACTIVE from DEPRECATED, and a compromised governance can install any admissible wrapper after the delay (the delay is the users' exit window, and the ECDSA floor still applies). The identity register and the recorded identity-at-queue (lifecycle, U-1) are design, not code.

candidates.name: direct stateless adapter (the current ZKMLDSAVerifier path)
candidates.summary: A tightly scoped stateless wrapper behind IPQCVerifier verifies the proof and binds four journal words to the digest, the credential, the chain and itself; the Vault binds the operation through the digest it computes and consumes the nonce atomically. This is what the repository has built (SP1-TD1 direct immutable verifier, SP1-TD2 halt).

analysis.trustMinimization: no key, no attester, no registry: soundness plus the consumer's own typed data
analysis.gas: one Groth16 verification (pairing precompile) plus two ABI decodes per PQ-gated operation; not measured in this lane
analysis.verifierLifecycle: per-consumer timelocked rotation with the halt as the only emergency control; no memory of deprecated identities
analysis.verifierKeyManagement: none: PROGRAM_VKEY and the code-hash pin are immutable constants, changed only by deploying a new wrapper
analysis.upgradeRisk: clean cutover (verifierAddress word), but downgrade to any non-halted identity is possible through governance
analysis.calldataSize: 160-byte journal plus about 260 bytes of Groth16 proof plus ABI framing, per operation
analysis.failureModes: every failure is false at the wrapper and a revert at the Vault; nothing is written on failure
analysis.operationalComplexity: lowest: no state beyond the Vault's nonce

candidates.name: verification adapter with an on-chain evidence registry
candidates.summary: An isolated verifier contract validates the proof and records a canonical evidence commitment (digest, pkHash, identity) that the Vault later consumes in a separate transaction.

analysis.separationOfConcerns: clean on paper, but the Vault already separates verification (IPQCVerifier) from authorization
analysis.replaySemantics: needs its own consumption rule in the registry on top of the Vault's nonce: two nullifiers for one operation
analysis.registryPoisoning: anyone with a valid proof writes entries; entries for operations that will never execute accumulate and must be reasoned about
analysis.atomicity: two transactions: the proof is verified in one and consumed in another, so the identity that verified may be deprecated or revoked before consumption
analysis.staleEvidence: an entry outlives the policy, mode and identity under which it was written; the Vault would have to re-check all of them anyway
analysis.upgradeBoundaries: registry state survives verifier identities and needs identity tagging and migration
analysis.authorizationSurface: a second contract whose storage decides authorization; its upgrade path becomes a custody dependency

candidates.name: off-chain verification with on-chain attestation
candidates.summary: An off-chain service verifies the SP1 proof (or the ML-DSA signature directly) and signs an attestation the Vault accepts; the repository's AttestationPQCVerifier / ImmutableAttestationPQCVerifier path.

analysis.signerTrust: the attester is a sole external authenticator for the PQ conjunct: whoever holds its key authorizes whatever it attests, violating I-NO-SOLE-EXTERNAL-AUTHENTICATOR for that conjunct
analysis.keyCompromise: total for the PQ leg; under Hybrid the ECDSA floor survives, which is exactly the floor's job and not a merit of this candidate
analysis.liveness: a down attester halts every PQ-gated operation; censorship is one key away
analysis.replay: attestations need their own nonce and domain binding, duplicating the Vault's
analysis.operationalBurden: key custody, rotation, monitoring: runtime infrastructure this design must not introduce
analysis.purpose: it defeats the purpose of the SP1 proof: an attester trusted to verify a proof could be trusted to verify the ML-DSA signature directly, and the proof adds nothing on chain

candidates.name: stateless adapter as the PQ conjunct of the vNext Hybrid floor, with an identity register
candidates.summary: Candidate A's stateless wrapper, consumed as the post-quantum conjunct behind the kernel's ecrecover floor (vNext section 4.3a, K-5), under the denial-only verifier plane (section 11) and the delayed lifecycle, plus a consumer-side identity register that gives every (codehash, vkey) identity one of the five lifecycle states, refuses DEPRECATED and REVOKED identities at proposal and apply, never returns from DEPRECATED to ACTIVE, and records the identity that admitted each queued operation.

analysis.trustMinimization: the PQ verdict can only deny: a compromised or unsound verifier cannot move funds while the floor holds
analysis.atomicity: verification and nonce consumption in one transaction, as in A
analysis.downgradeResistance: the register remembers deprecated identities, so a re-installation of an old program is refused (PB-7); the transition is one-way
analysis.upgradeSafety: propose, delay, re-check code at apply, expire (existing); plus identity states and the identity recorded at queue, so REVOKED can refuse finalization of what it admitted
analysis.compatibility: IPQCVerifier for the v1 Vault today, IKernelPQVerifier for the kernel; the wrapper is unchanged
analysis.cost: one register read at proposal and apply, one identity word stored per queued operation; the verification path is A's
analysis.whatIsNotBuilt: the register, the identity-at-queue record, the gates G-16 and G-17; all implementation-lane work

recommended.why: D keeps everything A already binds (one verification, one nonce, one transaction, immutable program identity, code-hash-pinned verifier) and adds the two things A lacks: a denial-only position for the PQ verdict behind a floor the kernel evaluates itself, and a memory of deprecated identities so that old programs cannot return. It introduces no key, no attester, no registry of evidence and no second nullifier. Its scores are never BLOCKING and its two ACCEPTABLE lifecycle scores are the parts not yet built, named as implementation-lane prerequisites. The evidence supports this choice because A is built and tested, the vNext invariants it stands on are adjudicated, and the register is a small addition whose invariants (PB-7, PB-13, PB-14) are already stated as executable tests.

rejected.why: Not rejected as a mechanism: D contains it. Not recommended alone because without the register a deprecated program can be re-installed through governance (T12) and without the floor the PQ verdict could become a sole authenticator in PqOnly, which generation 1 rejects.

Non-atomic by construction: a proof verified in one transaction and consumed in another lets the identity, policy and mode change in between, and the Vault would have to re-check all of them, leaving the registry as a second nullifier that only adds poisoning and migration surface. Nothing in the Vault needs an evidence commitment it did not compute itself.

BLOCKING on trust minimization, downgrade resistance and program identity: the attester's key is a sole external authenticator for the PQ conjunct, its compromise is total for that leg, its liveness is custody liveness, and an attester trusted to verify a proof could verify the signature directly, so the proof buys nothing. Ease is not a reason.

identity.programIdentity: PROGRAM_VKEY, SP1's verifying-key commitment to the designated ELF (designation mldsa65-withdrawal-d1: source commit, ELF sha256 2adddae7…, vkey 0x0001a4c6…); immutable per wrapper; a different program is a different wrapper.
identity.verifierIdentity: the wrapper's runtime identity keccak256(SP1_VERIFIER code hash, PROGRAM_VKEY), as VerifierRotationGuard computes it and WalletWallVault stores it in pqVerifierIdentity at install; SP1_VERIFIER itself is pinned to the v6.1.0 runtime code hash.
identity.consumerIdentity: each consumer (WalletWallVault, the multisig vault, the simulator, the policy bridge, a vNext kernel clone) holds one pqVerifier address and one identity at a time; identity state lives in the consumer's register, never in the wrapper.
identity.whoMayAdd: an identity enters PROPOSED when the consumer's governance (the contract owner; never the halt principal, which VerifierRotationGuard refuses as a principal) calls proposePQVerifier; it becomes QUALIFIED only with release evidence (designation, wrapper build fact in the append-only registry, two-host canonical rebuild, per-chain execution check, a fixture proof verified by the designated runtime); it becomes ACTIVE at applyPQVerifierUpdate after 172,800 s and a code re-check.
identity.whoMayRemove: governance deprecates (timelocked, one-way); the wrapper's HALT_PRINCIPAL revokes immediately and alone through halt(), which the guard turns into a refusal of that identity everywhere; nothing un-deprecates or un-revokes.
identity.emergencyRevoke: needed and present: halt() is one-way, immediate, consumer-wide through the guard, and its principal has no other power (denial only).
identity.downgrade: today possible to any non-halted identity through the rotation; the register makes DEPRECATED and REVOKED identities inadmissible at proposal and at apply, so a downgrade requires an identity that was never deprecated, which the lifecycle forbids for superseded programs.
identity.oldProofsAfterUpgrade: unconsumed proofs addressed to the old wrapper fail its verifierAddress word after apply (no grace period: a prover re-proves against the new wrapper); authorizations already consumed and queued finalize without re-verification unless their admitting identity is REVOKED, in which case the design requires finalization to refuse (U-1).
evidencePerChange: PQVerifierUpdateProposed(old, new, validAfter) and the apply event with the new pqVerifierIdentity (existing)
VerifierHalted from the wrapper (existing) and the guard's refusal of the halted identity (existing)
a designation record and a wrapper build fact in the append-only registry before QUALIFIED (existing formats, 0 facts today)
IdentityDeprecated / IdentityRevoked events from the consumer's register (design)
the identity recorded at queue for every queued operation (design)

publicValues.layout: static ABI tuple (bytes32, bytes32, bytes32, uint64, address): five 32-byte words, big-endian, left-padded, no length prefix, no dynamic part; produced by the guest, expected by scripts/prover-client.ts, decoded by ZKMLDSAVerifier.decodeProofPayload with ABI validation

fields.name: withdrawalDigest
fields.semantics: the consumer's EIP-712 digest of the operation (operationId)

fields.name: pkHash
fields.semantics: keccak256 of the ML-DSA-65 public key the signature verified under
fields.checkedBy: ZKMLDSAVerifier: committedPkHash == keccak256(publicKey), the consumer's registered credential

fields.name: sigHash
fields.semantics: keccak256 of the signature; bound by the proof, non-authoritative

fields.name: chainId
fields.semantics: the chain the proof is routed to; upper 192 bits must be zero (ABI validation)

fields.name: verifierAddress
fields.semantics: the wrapper deployment the proof is for; upper 96 bits must be zero (ABI validation)

digest.scheme: EIP-712 typed data, OpenZeppelin EIP712("WalletWallVault", "1"): digest = keccak256(0x1901 || domainSeparator || structHash)
digest.domain: EIP712Domain(name "WalletWallVault", version "1", chainId, verifyingContract = the Vault)
typeHashes: Withdrawal(address vaultOwner,address recipient,uint256 amount,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline,uint8 vaultMode)
RotateCredentials(address vaultOwner,address newEcdsaSigner,bytes newPQPublicKey,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)
digest.construction: the consumer computes the digest from the caller's typed request and its own domain; it is both the guest's private message input and the journal's first word; the guest signs it with an empty ML-DSA context string

proofPayload.abi: abi.encode(bytes publicValues, bytes proofBytes), passed as the IPQCVerifier `proof` argument; decoded by an external pure function so malformed offsets become false, not a revert
proofPayload.selector: proofBytes[0:4] == bytes4(VERIFIER_HASH) = 0x4388a21c for SP1Verifier v6.1.0; the verifier reverts on any other selector

verifierBinding.programVKey: verifyProof(PROGRAM_VKEY, publicValues, proofBytes): the vkey is the first Groth16 public input
verifierBinding.publicValuesDigest: sha256(publicValues) masked to 253 bits is the second Groth16 public input (upstream SP1VerifierGroth16.hashPublicValues; the verifier source is not vendored here, so this is an upstream-source statement consistent with NC-V3's observed refusal of altered public values), so the proof binds the exact 160 bytes; the wrapper's word comparisons bind those bytes to its context

domainSeparation: programs: PROGRAM_VKEY (a different guest is a different vkey; the ACVP guest cannot pay a withdrawal)
consumers, chains and typed-data versions: the EIP-712 domain separator inside the digest
operations: the type hash inside the struct hash
deployments: the chainId and verifierAddress journal words
forbidden: JSON or any self-describing serialization in the journal
dynamic-length fields or length-prefixed fields in the journal
implicit field order or field order by name
human-readable concatenation or decimal rendering of integers
a journal word that names its own program or version (circular; unverifiable)
a caller-supplied digest accepted by any consumer
encoding.nextGeneration: If the program changes for any other reason, generation 2 prepends a journal domain word bytes32 JOURNAL_DOMAIN = keccak256("walletwall.sp1.mldsa65-withdrawal.journal.v2") (192 bytes, six words) and may drop sigHash; a new journal layout is a new vkey and so a new identity, which enters the lifecycle at PROPOSED. No change to the journal is made by this lane or needed for the v1 layout, whose separation by vkey is sufficient.

replay.nullifier: the per-owner nonce inside the digest (vault.nonce for WalletWallVault); no separate consumed-proof registry, operation-hash set or one-time authorization id is needed, because a digest with a consumed nonce can never be recomputed by the Vault
replay.stateLocation: the consumer: VaultOwner.nonce per owner, and for queued operations the pending map keyed by operationId (the digest) with the recorded admitting policy engine and, by design, the admitting verifier identity
replay.consumedWhen: in the transaction that accepts the proof: withdraw and rotateCredentials consume at execution; queueWithdrawal consumes at queue, and finalizeWithdrawal later executes the stored request by operationId without re-verifying the proof
replay.atomicity: verification, nonce advance and execution (or queue write) are one transaction; a revert anywhere undoes all of them
replay.onRevert: nothing is consumed: the nonce, the pending map and the balance are unchanged, and the same proof remains usable
replay.retry: a proof may be resubmitted until its nonce is consumed or its deadline passes; a proof is never retried after a success because the nonce has advanced
replay.crossChain: chainId in the journal (wrapper check) and in the EIP-712 domain (digest); a chain-id fork voids the proof on both sides
replay.crossContract: verifyingContract in the EIP-712 domain and the consumer-computed digest (PB-11) separate consumers; verifierAddress in the journal separates wrapper deployments
replay.crossUser: vaultOwner in the struct and pkHash against the owner's registered credential
replay.deadline: request.deadline in the struct, checked block.timestamp <= deadline before the verifier is called; the only time binding

lifecycle.mapping: PROPOSED = proposePQVerifier called (pending, validAfter set); QUALIFIED = release evidence complete for the identity (designation, registry fact, two-host rebuild, per-chain check, fixture proof); ACTIVE = installed as pqVerifier after applyPQVerifierUpdate; DEPRECATED = superseded or declared deprecated by governance, refused for re-installation; REVOKED = halted by HALT_PRINCIPAL or revoked by governance, refused everywhere and, by design, refusing finalization of what it admitted. The current contracts implement PROPOSED, ACTIVE and (through halt) REVOKED; QUALIFIED is off-chain evidence today; DEPRECATED and the register are design.

states.meaning: an identity named by governance, waiting out the 172,800 s delay; or a program designated but not yet evidenced
states.proofBeforeTransitionExecutesAfter: not applicable: nothing executes through a proposed identity

states.meaning: release evidence complete: designation, append-only registry fact, two-host canonical rebuild, per-chain execution check, a fixture proof verified by the designated runtime, host qualification of the evidence hosts
states.proofBeforeTransitionExecutesAfter: a proof made while QUALIFIED executes once the identity is ACTIVE, provided its deadline and nonce still hold

states.meaning: installed as the consumer's pqVerifier; the only state in which a proof authorizes a new operation
states.proofBeforeTransitionExecutesAfter: a proof made under ACTIVE and not consumed before the identity leaves ACTIVE fails the verifierAddress word of the successor; it must be re-proved

states.meaning: no longer installed anywhere, or declared deprecated by governance (one-way break declaration, vNext section 12); refused at proposal and at apply
states.proofBeforeTransitionExecutesAfter: an operation already queued under this identity finalizes (its proof was consumed while ACTIVE); an unconsumed proof cannot execute

states.meaning: halted by HALT_PRINCIPAL (verify() returns false for every input) or revoked by governance; refused everywhere; finalization of operations it admitted is refused by design (U-1)
states.proofBeforeTransitionExecutesAfter: never: neither an unconsumed proof nor a queued operation admitted by a revoked identity executes

transitions.by: release evidence, verified by the validators in canonical CI
transitions.evidence: designation record, wrapper build fact in the append-only registry, two-host canonical rebuild record, per-chain execution check, fixture proof exercise record

transitions.by: governance withdraws the proposal (cancelPQVerifierUpdate) or the apply window expires
transitions.evidence: the cancel event or ProposalExpired; the register marks the identity withdrawn

transitions.by: governance: applyPQVerifierUpdate after the delay, with the target re-checked for code and against the register
transitions.evidence: PQVerifierUpdateProposed then the apply event; pqVerifierIdentity equals the qualified identity

transitions.by: governance declares the identity superseded before it was ever installed
transitions.evidence: IdentityDeprecated event and a registry fact

transitions.by: a successor becomes ACTIVE (rotation applied) or governance declares deprecation
transitions.evidence: the successor's apply event names the old identity; IdentityDeprecated event

transitions.by: HALT_PRINCIPAL calls halt() on the wrapper (immediate, one-way), or governance revokes in the register
transitions.evidence: VerifierHalted event; the guard refuses the identity; IdentityRevoked event

transitions.by: HALT_PRINCIPAL halt() or governance revoke, when a deprecated identity is found unsound

residues.name: measurement tool does not exit after writing; killed by the observer guard
residues.finding: scripts/measure-sp1-attributed-proof-exercise.ts keeps a readline interface open on stdin after writing its observation; the observer's 600 s guard SIGKILLs it and prints a misleading 'no observation is written' line although the file was written and verified byte-for-byte.
residues.why: The defect is in the lane's measurement tooling, after the observation is written; it touches no proof byte, no verification and no on-chain component, so it cannot affect Layers A to C or any binding this design defines. It must be fixed before the next attributed proving exercise, because a future host-qualification gate cannot rest on a tool that ends by SIGKILL.
residues.boundary: No further attributed proving exercise is run with the unfixed tool; the fix (close the readline, exit 0 after the write) and a regression test belong to the lane that next needs the tool, not to production binding.

residues.name: Docker Desktop ran during the proof
residues.finding: The Docker Desktop service VM was active on the proving host; its initd and rpc.idmapd sent 3 packets to 192.168.65.x over vsock from another network namespace, counted as otherNamespaceEgress = 3 in the record.
residues.why: Production binding does not rely on prover-host hermeticity: a proof is sound or it is not, independent of what else ran on the host (T13). The sends were observed, counted and attributed to the VM, not to the prover. For release evidence the relevant host property is build reproducibility across two independent hosts, which digest equality establishes regardless of co-resident services.
residues.boundary: PA3D is described as CONTINUOUS_PARTIALLY_ATTRIBUTED, never as hermetic; the two-host rebuild, not host hygiene, is the reproducibility evidence.

residues.name: partial process and network attribution (19 / 10 / 3)
residues.finding: 19 unattributed kernel events (IPv6 MLD/ND/RS around the gnark container's veth), 10 dockerd packet-socket sends of unseen destination inside the container namespace, 3 Docker Desktop other-namespace sends; 0 unknown outcomes; 237 refused packets.
residues.why: The residue bears on Layer D (how confidently one exercise's egress is attributed), not on Layers A to C, which the on-chain verifier establishes without reference to any host. Every count is recorded and bounded; nothing left the VM unrefused. The design places prover provenance outside the production statement on purpose.
residues.boundary: Attribution evidence is release evidence for the exercise, never an input to verify(); a future gate may require COMPLETE attribution for release-evidence hosts, and that is a host-qualification decision, not a binding one.

residues.name: chronyd activity, observed and refused
residues.finding: chronyd made 54 time-sync attempts inside the window; all were refused by the boundary; the host clock ran free during the exercise.
residues.why: The statement has no time input (timestamp is MUST_NOT_BIND; the deadline is the consumer's), so no clock on the proving host can influence what the proof binds. The record's timestamps order the manifest before the proof on one monotone host clock, which the refused sync attempts did not adjust.
residues.boundary: Timestamps in exercise records are informational ordering evidence, never authorization inputs.

residues.name: acquisition gate does not bind the Node dependency tree
residues.finding: The exercise manifest digests the guest ELF, the fixture inputs, the circuit archive and the gnark image, but not package-lock.json nor the installed node_modules that run the prover client, the verification script and the record validators.
residues.why: An unpinned dependency tree is a supply-chain path into the evidence (expected public values, verification observations, validator verdicts), though not into the on-chain verifier. Before any identity may become QUALIFIED on release evidence, the manifests and host qualification must bind the lock file's digest and the integrity-verified install (npm ci) that produced the evidence, and CI must refuse drift (G-20).
residues.boundary: Not required before the implementation lane, whose tests run in CI from the locked tree; required before release evidence is trusted for QUALIFIED.

residues.name: PA3D validators not wired into canonical CI
residues.finding: ci.yml runs validate:sp1-pin-parity, -host-advisories, -wrapper-build, -designation, -registry, -proving-availability, -impl-receipt, -circuit-tooling and -input, but not validate:sp1-pa3d-manifest or validate:sp1-pa3d-record; their logic reaches CI only through the mocha suite's PA3D tests.
residues.why: The implementation lane consumes the PA3D record and this design manifest as its baseline; if the standalone validators (and validate:sp1-pa3e-design) do not run in canonical CI, the baseline can drift without a red check. Wiring them is an edit to .github/workflows/ci.yml, which the publishing App cannot push (no workflows permission), so it is an owner act.
residues.boundary: Until wired, the mocha suite's Sp1Pa3dRecord and Sp1Pa3eDesign tests are the only CI enforcement; they validate the committed files but do not exercise the npm entry points.

residues.name: canonical release rebuild on two hosts unmet
residues.finding: The implementation receipt's CANONICAL_RELEASE_REBUILD_TWO_HOSTS prerequisite is unmet (INSUFFICIENT_HOSTS): one build's ELF digest stands behind the designation.
residues.why: Source-commit substitution (T17) is closed only by reproducibility: a second independent host must rebuild the designated source to the designated ELF sha256 and vkey before the identity may be QUALIFIED (PB-18).
residues.boundary: A lifecycle condition on QUALIFIED, not on this design or on the implementation lane's tests.

gates.reference: WalletWallVault computes _hashTypedDataV4 at every site; a structural test over every IPQCVerifier consumer (like Sp1Td2VerifierRotation's 'the source assigns pqVerifier only in…') is MISSING

invariants.statement: A proof generated for another chain cannot authorize this Vault: the journal's chainId word and the EIP-712 domain's chainId both differ.
invariants.enforcedToday: ZKMLDSAVerifier full-width chain id check (F-1); 'refuses a journal committing another chain id'

invariants.statement: A proof generated for another Vault cannot authorize this Vault: verifyingContract is in the digest and the Vault computes the digest itself.
invariants.enforcedToday: mechanism in WalletWallVault (_hashTypedDataV4); explicit two-Vault test MISSING (G-13)

invariants.statement: A proof for another recipient cannot authorize the intended transaction: recipient is in the digest and the Vault pays the field it hashed.
invariants.enforcedToday: 'one observed withdrawal signature cannot authorize a different withdrawal'

invariants.statement: A proof for another amount cannot authorize the intended transaction: amount is in the digest and the Vault transfers the field it hashed.
A proof against an unauthorized program cannot authorize execution: PROGRAM_VKEY is the Groth16 public input, immutable per wrapper, and only an ACTIVE identity is installed.
A valid proof cannot execute more than once: the digest commits a per-owner nonce consumed in the accepting transaction.
invariants.enforcedToday: InvalidNonce paths; 'fail on replay with the same nonce'

invariants.statement: A DEPRECATED or REVOKED identity cannot authorize new operations: it is refused at proposal and apply, DEPRECATED never returns to ACTIVE, and a halted wrapper verifies nothing.
invariants.enforcedToday: halt and guard refusal exist; DEPRECATED and the register are design (G-16, G-17)

invariants.statement: Changing any security-relevant public input invalidates authorization: the proof binds sha256 of the whole journal and the wrapper compares digest, pkHash, chainId and verifierAddress to its context.
Verifier failure or ambiguity fails closed: every non-success path of verify() is false, every false is a Vault revert, and no state is written on failure.
invariants.enforcedToday: try/catch in verify(); 'rejects a withdrawal if the SP1 verifier fails'; 'returns false for malformed ABI proof payloads'

invariants.statement: The on-chain operation consumed is cryptographically bound to the statement proven: the Vault executes exactly the typed request whose digest it verified, and queued operations finalize from the stored request under that digest.
invariants.enforcedToday: WalletWallVault execution from request fields; queued-path relation-consumer tests

invariants.statement: Every consumer computes the digest it passes to the verifier from its own typed data and domain; no function accepts a caller-supplied digest.
invariants.enforcedToday: true of WalletWallVault by inspection; a structural test over all IPQCVerifier consumers is MISSING (G-03)

invariants.statement: Every operation field a consumer executes (recipient, amount, asset where any, new credentials) is a field of the typed struct hashed into the digest.
invariants.enforcedToday: true of WalletWallVault's two structs; a requirement on any multi-asset consumer

invariants.statement: In generation 1 the PQ verdict is never the sole authenticator: the consumer evaluates its own ECDSA floor regardless of the PQ result (Hybrid; PqOnly rejected; I-NO-SOLE-EXTERNAL-AUTHENTICATOR).
invariants.enforcedToday: vNext section 4.3a adjudication and the kernel prototype's K-5 floor; WalletWallVault still offers PqOnly, which the production candidate must not

invariants.statement: The verifier plane is denial-only: no verifier identity, state, transition or failure can move funds, change ownership or widen authorization.
invariants.enforcedToday: halt() has no other power; rotation installs only; vNext section 11

invariants.statement: Policy is not a proof input: admission is decided at check and revalidate by the engine current at execution, and no journal field describes policy.
invariants.enforcedToday: the journal has no policy word; revalidate is fail-closed STATICCALL

invariants.statement: Public values are a fixed-width static ABI tuple whose length and word validity the consumer checks before any cryptographic verification, and whose canonical form three independent implementations (guest, TypeScript, Solidity) agree on.
invariants.enforcedToday: length and ABI-validated decode exist; the committed three-way fixture test is PARTIAL (G-02)

invariants.statement: Every identity change is observable: each lifecycle transition emits an event and has an off-chain evidence record before it takes effect.
invariants.enforcedToday: proposal, apply and halt events exist; register events are design

invariants.statement: No identity becomes QUALIFIED until the designated source rebuilds to the designated ELF and vkey on two independent hosts.

unresolved.question: Should a REVOKED identity refuse finalization of large withdrawals it admitted while ACTIVE? The design says yes (record the admitting identity at queue, like policyEngineAtQueue, and refuse at finalize); the owner confirms, since it changes which queued operations a halt stops.

Which consumer is the production candidate for generation 1: WalletWallVault (IPQCVerifier, offers PqOnly) or the vNext kernel (IKernelPQVerifier, Hybrid floor, PqOnly rejected)? The design binds the same statement through either; PB-13 requires the latter's floor rule wherever the binding goes live.
Does the next program generation drop the unchecked sigHash word and add the journal domain word? Only when another change forces a new vkey; no change is proposed for v1.
What is the measured gas of the full PQ-gated path on Base and Ethereum? Not measured in this lane; required as release evidence (G-23) before any ACTIVE identity.
Which second host performs the canonical rebuild (INSUFFICIENT_HOSTS)? A resource decision; a lifecycle condition on QUALIFIED, not on the design.

Does the register live in each consumer or in one shared contract? The design places it in the consumer (identity state is a consumer decision; a shared register would be a shared authority the vNext planes forbid); the implementation lane confirms against gas and clone-factory constraints.

nonGoals: no Solidity is modified and no production verifier behaviour changes
SP1 verification is not activated in production; no identity becomes QUALIFIED or ACTIVE by this lane
no Vault custody or withdrawal-authorization semantic changes; the statement is the existing IPQCVerifier.verify contract
nothing is deployed; no proof is generated (none was needed to answer a design question); no hosted proving
no secrets, signing keys, runtime infrastructure or telemetry are added
no claim of quantum-safe production custody and no claim of production SP1 binding: PRODUCTION_SP1_BINDING = NOT_ESTABLISHED
the resulting PR is a draft, auto-merge off, never merged by this lane; the implementation lane is not begun
PA3D is not called hermetic; no PA3D fact is downgraded
implementationPrerequisites: owner act: wire validate:sp1-pa3d-manifest, validate:sp1-pa3d-record and validate:sp1-pa3e-design into ci.yml (PA3D-VALIDATORS-NOT-IN-CI; the App cannot push workflow edits)
owner decisions: U-1 (REVOKED refuses finalization), U-2 (production consumer), U-5 (second rebuild host)

begin with the smallest executable invariant tests against the existing contracts: PB-1..PB-6, PB-8..PB-12 as Solidity tests, including the missing two-Vault test (G-13) and the structural consumer-computed-digest test (G-03)
then the register interface and its tests (PB-7, PB-17, G-16, G-17) and the identity-at-queue record, without touching the wrapper
the committed three-way encoding fixture test (G-02, PB-16)
bind the Node dependency tree into exercise manifests and host qualification (PA3D-ACQUISITION-NODE-TREE, G-20) before any release evidence is trusted for QUALIFIED
fix PA3D-F1 before the next attributed proving exercise; the two-host canonical rebuild (G-22, PB-18) and the gas measurement (G-23) before any identity is QUALIFIED
no broad Solidity rewrite: the wrapper and the Vault's authorization semantics are unchanged by the recommended architecture
